methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ark Electronics operates in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector at an undisclosed stage. The comparable universe comprises one publicly traded peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private companies, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. This modest peer set reflects the nascent and heterogeneous nature of frontier robotics investment.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The analysis identified eleven same-sector peers overall, but filtering by stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort—below the minimum threshold for reliable median-based inference. An all-sector median approach would obscure material differences in capital intensity, commercialization maturity, and addressable market between Ark Electronics and peers operating at divergent development phases.

Without sufficient stage-matched or tier-matched comparables, triangulation across revenue multiples, EV/EBITDA, or precedent transaction analysis cannot be conducted with confidence. The analysis does not support a specific valuation range at this time. Key uncertainties include Ark Electronics' precise development stage, revenue traction, capital deployment to date, and technical differentiation relative to the fragmented peer set. A defensible valuation would require either (1) narrowing the peer set through validated stage and metric alignment, or (2) employing alternative methods such as DCF analysis anchored to disclosed financial performance or market sizing assumptions.
